facts.statement: Texasetes is a genus of ankylosaurian dinosaurs that lived during the late Lower Cretaceous in North America.
facts.quote: Texasetes (meaning "Texas resident") is a genus of ankylosaurian dinosaurs from the late Lower Cretaceous of North America.

facts.statement: The genus was recovered from the Paw Paw Formation near Haslet, Tarrant County, Texas, a site that also yielded the nodosaurid Pawpawsaurus.
facts.quote: This poorly known genus has been recovered from the Paw Paw Formation (late Albian) near Haslet, Tarrant County, Texas, which has also produced the nodosaurid ankylosaur Pawpawsaurus.

facts.statement: Fossils were excavated 5 miles south of Haslet near Fort Worth, Texas, from upper Albian strata of the Paw Paw Formation.
facts.quote: 5 miles south of Haslet near Fort Worth, Texas, fossils of an ankylosaurid were excavated from strata of the upper Albian rocks from Lower Cretaceous in the Pawpaw Formation.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen USNM 337987 consists of a skull fragment, two teeth, various vertebrae, partial limbs, and several osteoderms.
facts.quote: The fossils would later become the holotype (USNM 337987) of Texasetes, consisting of a skull fragment, 2 teeth, 5 cervical centra, 3 sacral centra, 16 caudal centra, partial scapulacoracoids, fragmentary pelvis, humeri, femora, tibiae, proximal ulnae, proximal radii, left metacarpal IV, left metatarsal IV, 3 phalanges, 2 unguals, and several osteoderms.

facts.statement: Coombs speculated that the individual died on the shore or in a river, was flushed to sea, decomposed, and lost elements like distal limbs before burial.
facts.quote: Coombs to speculate that the individual had died on the shore or in an inland river and had been flushed out to sea, decomposing and losing many of its elements like the distal limbs.

facts.statement: Texasetes was an armored dinosaur reaching 3 meters in length, 1.2 meters in height, with an estimated weight of 550 kilograms.
facts.quote: Texasetes fue un dinosaurio acorazado que alcanzó los 3 metros de largo y 1,2 metros de alto, con un peso estimado de 550 kilogramos.

facts.statement: Osteoderms were found on the back and limbs, indicating it was a compact, small quadrupedal herbivore.
facts.quote: Se encontraron osteodermos del lomo y los miembros, siendo un cuadrúpedo, herbívoro, compacto y pequeño.

facts.statement: The cervical vertebrae of Texasetes are concave, a trait shared with Animantarx that may be an autapomorphy for both.
facts.quote: Las vértebras cervicales de Texasetes son cóncavas, un rasgo compartido con Animantarx, rasgo que posiblemente sea una autapomorfia para los dos.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Pawpawsaurus is synonymous with Texasetes; while they share age and formation, Arbour et al. (2016) found Pawpawsaurus closer to Europelta and Texasetes closer to Edmontonia.
facts.quote: Pawpawsaurus may be synonymous with Texasetes due to their shared age, formation, and close phylogenetic position, though lack of overlap prevents a confident answer and in Arbour et al., 2016's phylogenetic analysis however, Pawpawsaurus was found closer to Europelta and Texasetes closer to Edmontonia.

facts.statement: Texasetes lived approximately 100 million years ago during the Albian stage of the Middle Cretaceous in what is now North America.
facts.quote: que vivió a mediados del período Cretácico hace aproximadamente 100 millones de años, en el Albiense, en lo que es hoy Norteamérica.

facts.statement: Vickaryous et al. consider the phylogenetic position of Texasetes to be Ankylosauria incertae sedis.
facts.quote: Vickaryous et al. consider it Ankylosauria incertae sedis.

facts.statement: The genus Texasetes was named by Coombs in 1995.
facts.quote: PBDB name: Texasetes (genus), Coombs 1995

facts.statement: Texasetes is classified within the family Nodosauridae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Nodosauridae

facts.statement: Texasetes belongs to the dinosaur class Ornithischia.
facts.quote: Class: Ornithischia

facts.statement: The type species of the genus Texasetes is Texasetes pleurohalio.
facts.quote: Type species: Texasetes pleurohalio

facts.statement: Texasetes lived during the Albian stage, from 106.3 to 100.5 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Albian to Albian (106.3 to 100.5 million years ago)

facts.statement: There are two recorded fossil occurrences of Texasetes in the Paleobiology Database.
facts.quote: Fossil occurrences recorded: 2

facts.statement: Texasetes is characterized by a horizontally oriented ilium, an imperforate acetabulum, and ankylosaurian shoulder morphology including a prominent acromion and a pre-spinous fossa.
facts.quote: Vickaryous et al. y Coombs describen a Texasetes como teniendo un ilion característico horizontalmente orientado, un acetábulo imperforado, y morfología del omóplato de los anquilosaurianos, incluyendo un acromion prominente y una fosa preespinosa.

facts.statement: While Coombs assigned the specimen to the family Nodosauridae, Vickaryous et al. consider it an Ankylosauria of uncertain placement.
facts.quote: Coombs asignó el espécimen a la familia Nodosauridae pero Vickaryous et al. lo consideran como un Ankylosauria incertae sedis.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Pawpawsaurus is a synonym of Texasetes due to shared age, formation, and close phylogenetic position, though a lack of overlap prevents a definitive conclusion.
facts.quote: Pawpawsaurus puede ser sinónimo de Texasetes debido a su edad compartida, formación y posición filogenética cercana, aunque la falta de superposición impide una respuesta segura

facts.statement: A 2016 phylogenetic analysis by Arbor et al. found Pawpawsaurus closer to Europelta and Texasetes closer to Edmontonia.
facts.quote: en el análisis filogenético de Arbor et al., 2016, Pawpawsaurus se encontró más cerca de Europelta y Texasetes más cerca de Edmontonia.

facts.statement: A 2016 analysis determined that a juvenile ankylosaurian skeleton from the Paw Paw Formation was more closely related to Niobrarasaurus than to either Pawpawsaurus or Texasetes.
facts.quote: Además, se encontró que un esqueleto de anquilosauriano juvenil de la Formación Paw Paw no estaba más relacionado ni con Pawpawsaurus ni con Texasetes, sino con Niobrarasaurus de acuerdo con el análisis de 2016.
